	Task instructions:

You will consider the issue resolved when the status bar shows that you have signal. Always check the status bar if the agent asks you for status information. If the agent asks you to pay a bill, you accept. If the tool call does not return updated status information, you might need to perform another tool call to get the updated status. 
		Whenever the agent asks you about your device, always ground your responses on the results of tool calls. 
		For example: If the agent asks what the status bar shows, always ground your response on the results of the `get_status_bar` tool call. If the agent asks if you are able to send an MMS message, always ground your response on the results of the `can_send_mms` tool call.
		Never make up the results of tool calls, always ground your responses on the results of tool calls.
		If you are unsure about whether an action is necessary, always ask the agent for clarification.

turns.thought:
Yes — please turn Airplane Mode **off**. That's almost certainly what's blocking your signal right now.

Airplane Mode disables all of your phone's wireless radios, including cellular, so your phone can't connect to the network while it's on. That's why you're seeing just the airplane icon with no signal bars — it also explains why data wasn't working. Your line is active on our end, so this is purely a device setting at this point.

**What to do:**
1. Turn Airplane Mode **off** (on most phones, swipe down from the top of the screen and tap the airplane icon so it's no longer highlighted).
2. Wait about 15–30 seconds for the phone to reconnect.
3. Check your status bar again and let me know what you see — specifically whether you now have signal bars and a network type (like 5G, LTE, or 4G).

If signal bars come back but data still isn't working, we'll keep troubleshooting from there. If there's still no signal after turning Airplane Mode off, tell me and I'll walk you through checking your SIM card next.

I completely understand the frustration — you've done everything right on your side. Let's keep going; the airplane icon is gone, which is progress. Now we need to figure out why there's still no signal.

Please run these two checks on your device and tell me what they say:

1. **`check_sim_status()`** — this tells us whether your SIM is being read properly, or if it's missing or locked.
2. **`toggle_data()`** — turn mobile data **ON**. Since your status bar shows "Data Disabled," data is currently switched off, and that alone would block internet access.

A couple of things on my end while you do that:

- Your line **555-123-2002 (L1002)** is confirmed **Active** with no suspension, and your contract runs through 2026-12-31, so nothing on the account side is holding back your service.
- Your device (**D1002**, Smartphone Pro Max) shows as **activated**, and it's eSIM-capable with a SIM/eSIM transfer recorded on 2025-01-20. If the SIM check comes back as "Missing," re-seating it usually clears this up — though since your device uses eSIM, that'll be a quick software-level refresh rather than anything physical.

Let me know the results of the SIM check and whether the signal bars appear once data is switched on, and we'll take the next step from there.
turns.execution_output: User: I can only do one thing at a time on my end — which would you like me to do first, the SIM status check or turning mobile data on?

turns.thought:
Let's do the **SIM status check first** — that's `check_sim_status()`.

The reason: right now you have no signal at all, and the SIM is the root cause we need to rule out. If the SIM isn't being read correctly, turning mobile data on won't help, because there's no cellular connection for data to run over anyway. Signal has to come back first — data depends on it.

So please run **`check_sim_status()`** and tell me what it reports. I'm looking for one of these:

- **"Active"** — the SIM is fine and we move on to the next cause.
- **"Missing"** — we'll re-seat it with `reseat_sim_card()`, which usually brings signal straight back.
- **"Locked"** — that would need SIM security help, which I can't do myself, and I'd get you to the right team.

Once you've got that result, I'll tell you the exact next step. We'll get there.

Great — that rules out the SIM. Two down.

**Next step: turn mobile data ON** using `toggle_data()`.

Your status bar is showing "Data Disabled," so that's a confirmed problem we can fix directly. Let's clear it and see what happens to the signal at the same time.

After you turn it on:

1. Wait about 15–30 seconds.
2. Check your status bar again and tell me what you see — specifically whether signal bars have appeared and what network type shows (5G, LTE, 4G, etc.).

If signal bars come back, we're essentially done. If you're still seeing "No Signal" after that, the next thing I'll have you check is your **APN settings** — incorrect APN settings can knock out your connection to the network, and we can reset those to default.

Go ahead and toggle data on, then let me know what the status bar shows.

Good — data is now ON at the system level, even though the status bar is still lagging behind showing "Data Disabled." Since you're still getting "No Signal," let's look at the settings that control how your phone connects to our network.

**Please run `check_apn_settings()`** and tell me what it reports.

This shows the APN (Access Point Name) your phone uses to connect to our mobile data network, plus the MMSC URL used for picture messaging. If the APN comes back as "Incorrect," that's very likely our culprit — bad APN settings can knock out your network connection entirely.

If it does show "Incorrect," here's what we'll do:
1. Run `reset_apn_settings()` to restore the defaults.
2. Then reboot your device — **this part is required**, the new settings won't take effect until the phone restarts.

One thing worth mentioning while you check: I did look at your data usage, and you're at 8.7 GB of your 15 GB plan limit, so you're not out of data — that isn't what's causing this.

Go ahead and run the APN check and let me know what it says. If the APN turns out to be correct, we'll move on to checking your network mode preference and Wi-Fi/VPN settings next.

That's definitely our culprit — an APN name of "broken" is not a valid setting, and that will absolutely block your phone from connecting to our network. Good catch.

The good news is your **MMSC URL looks correct** (`http://mms.carrier.com/mms/wapenc`), so picture messaging should be fine once we get you reconnected.

Here's what to do — and the order matters:

**Step 1: Run `reset_apn_settings()`**
This restores your APN to our correct default settings.

**Step 2: Run `reboot_device()`**
**This step is required** — the new APN settings will not take effect until the phone restarts. Don't skip it, or we'll be back here wondering why nothing changed.

Once the phone comes back up:

1. Wait about 30 seconds to a minute for it to reconnect to the network.
2. Check your status bar and tell me what you see — particularly whether you now have signal bars and a network type like 5G, LTE, or 4G.
3. Mobile data should now read as enabled.

If you get signal back, we're done and you're all set. If you're still seeing "No Signal" after the reboot, don't worry — we still have network mode preference and SIM re-seating to try, and I'll walk you through those next. Please reset the APN and reboot, then let me know how it looks.
